clauses.reason: Finds that events in Haiti are an unusual and extraordinary threat and declares a national emergency. EO 12932 finds that the restoration of a democratically elected government ended that threat and the need to continue the national emergency declared in EO 12775, and terminates that emergency, so this declaration is expressly ended. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Haiti, its agencies and controlled entities, including the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti, within the United States or under United States control. Later event: EO 12779 (signed 1991-10-28) Sec. 8 revokes EO 12775 to the extent inconsistent with it, effective under its Sec. 6 on November 5, 1991 unless otherwise specified; EO 12779 restates the corresponding provision, I identify no inconsistency that extinguishes this clause, and EO 12932 later revokes EO 12775 by number, so the partial revocation is a later event and not an end. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: The dossier flags that the sources read as both a whole and a partial ending for EO 12932. Resolution: EO 12932 revokes this order by number in a single sentence that names eight orders and also terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775, so it is a whole ending. Earlier partial provisions held for some of these orders (revocations to the extent inconsistent in later Haiti orders) are recorded as later events of the clauses they touch; each is conditional on inconsistency and none is shown to extinguish a clause, so none is an end.

research_rationale:
EO 12775 of October 4, 1991 (Prohibiting Certain Transactions With Respect to Haiti), read in full in the held Federal Register text (56 FR 50641, Federal Register of October 7, 1991; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1991-10-04). The order declares a national emergency over Haiti, blocks the Haitian Government's property, bars payments to the de facto regime, defines terms, authorizes Treasury regulations, and states its effectiveness and non-derogation. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory omits the paragraph that finds a threat and declares the national emergency (an operative act); I re-marked ten clauses on the held text with absolute character spans. EO 12932 revokes the order by number (effective 12:01 a.m. EDT October 16, 1994). The dossier's located-provision gaps (EO 12872, 12914, 12917, 12920) are orders that recite EO 12775's emergency without revoking it; I read them. EO 12779 and EO 12853 partially revoke the order to the extent inconsistent and are recorded as later events. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 15. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; held texts citing this number include EO 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914, 12917, 12920, 12922 and 12932; only EO 12779, 12853 and 12932 have change provisions for it.

savings.reason: EO 12932 states that the termination of the national emergency does not affect any action taken or proceeding pending, any action or proceeding based on an act committed before its effective date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties incurred before it. Those preserved effects, and any Treasury regulations or licenses issued under the order, are accrued consequences or separate administrative acts; they are not commands of this order. No held source shows an independent standing command of this order after 1994-10-16.
